title: A WAN port is down: which, is it alerting, what is on the other end, since when, and its bill

turns.user: Which ports on edge-rtr1 are down?
turns.answer: Both WAN ports of `edge-rtr1.example.net`: `Gi0/0/0 (WAN: transit-a)` has been down for `2h 5m`, and `Gi0/0/1 (WAN: transit-b)` for `over 50d 0h`, since the router booted. Both are administratively up, so LibreNMS counts them as down. That is as of `2026-10-28T12:00:00Z`.

Yes. `Port down` on `Gi0/0/0` has been active since `2026-10-28T10:02:00Z` (`1h 58m`), and nobody has acknowledged it. The one on transit-b was acknowledged: `2026-10-28 09:15:00 - Ack (alice) carrier ticket 4411`.

turns.user: What is on the other end of transit-a?
turns.answer: `transit-a-pe1`, port `xe-0/0/1`, which says it is a `Juniper MX204`. LibreNMS does not monitor it, so I cannot see that side: the name and port are what the neighbour advertises about itself.

turns.user: When exactly did it go down?
turns.answer: The eventlog has it going `down` at `2026-10-28T09:55:00Z`, `2h 5m` ago, with no change since.

turns.user: Has it done that before this month?
turns.answer: Once more in the last 30 days: `Interface went down: Gi0/0/0` at `2026-10-20T14:05:00Z`.

turns.user: How close is that circuit to its commit?
turns.answer: The `Transit A` bill on that port has a 95th percentile of `812 Mbit/s` against a `1 Gbit/s` commit: `81.2` % of it this period (`2026-10-01` to `2026-10-31`), as LibreNMS last worked it out at `2026-10-28T11:50:02Z`.
